- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment spikes to 1.00, model often overreacts with sharp upward overshoots; cap or dampen forecast peaks to avoid overcorrection.
- Model frequently underestimates true values in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–5 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative — adjust upward by 10–20% for short-term bias.
- In high-sentiment periods (≥0.67), model often overestimates later periods (e.g., 10–30 days) — apply downward correction for long-term horizon if sentiment is sustained.
- If true outcome shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >30% from prior day), model often fails to catch it — add lagged sentiment momentum as a trigger to preemptively raise forecast.
- When sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model tends to misalign with trend direction — use sentiment polarity as a smoothing filter to reduce oscillation bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates volatility in high-sentiment periods — reduce forecast variance by 15–30% if sentiment >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days.
